summary: Tunnel-diode resonator measurements of magnetic susceptibility reveal that Ta films with lower microwave quality factors ($Q_i$) exhibit non-activated, non-exponential low-temperature behavior indicating subgap spectral weight, while Ta deposited on a 5 nm Nb interlayer shows clean activated response consistent with a fully gapped spectrum. The superconducting-state quasiparticle spectrum correlates with device performance, with the Nb interlayer dramatically improving both the gap structure and interface quality.
motivation: Understanding microscopic dissipation mechanisms in Ta-based superconducting qubits requires characterization methods beyond microwave measurements; Ta film performance is known to be sensitive to Ta/substrate interfaces, but the underlying quasiparticle spectrum has not been directly measured.
method: Magnetic susceptibility $\chi(T)$ was measured in the Meissner state using a precision frequency-domain tunnel-diode resonator at $\sim 10$ MHz across three sample types: 100 nm Ta on c-plane sapphire (type A), 95 nm Ta on 5 nm Nb/sapphire (type B), and 100 nm Ta on Ar-plasma-treated sapphire (type C); low-temperature behavior was analyzed via power-law fits to extract exponent $n$ and inverse susceptibility changes.
result: Type-B samples show exponentially activated low-$T$ response with power-law exponent $n > 6$ and $\Delta\chi$ two orders of magnitude smaller than lower-$Q_i$ types, while type-A and type-C samples display non-exponential temperature dependence with bumps and downturns, indicating the presence of Yu-Shiba-Rusinov states or two-level system-induced subgap states that correlate with reduced quality factors.
